wordline_capacitance_source: A DECLARED EXPECTATION, cross-checked, not the source of the number. The value used is read at run time from results/spice/ihp_sg13g2_rom_read_energy/read_energy.json#wordline_capacitance.ff_per_column; the run refuses if it disagrees with the value here by more than `wordline_capacitance_tolerance`. This contract used to carry the literal 0.5424 fF/column and cite that directory, which recorded no such quantity at all -- the citation could not be checked and the number was ungrounded. Changing the number here is only legitimate as a response to a new measurement, never to make a run pass.

establishes: that a via1-programmed mask-ROM bit array drawn at the minimum legal pitch requires periodic substrate tap bands, because without them the array violates the public latch-up rule LU.b
the drawn macro footprint of that array including tap bands, the wordline strap and the bitline escape, measured from the Magic-written LEF
the routed die area of that macro with a synthesised standard-cell periphery, under full OpenROAD place-and-route with zero detailed-route violations

the array efficiency at the contract's requested utilization, and the array efficiency at the tightest die of the same netlist that still closes detailed routing, which is a measured floor rather than a chosen one
forbidden_inferences: N7, N6, N5 or N4 macro area, array efficiency, density or timing
that a standard-cell periphery is equivalent to a memory-compiler periphery: it is not, and the measured efficiency is therefore a LOWER bound
sense-amplifier design, read margin, redundancy, BIST or test coverage, none of which is in this periphery
whole-wafer inference throughput or GPU speedup
the array efficiency of a die smaller than the tightest one probed: the floor probe brackets the die area, it does not minimise it

a die floor independent of the placer's target placement density: that density is a constant chosen in tools/run_ihp_rom_macro_route.py, the probe escalates it through `die_floor_probe_place_densities` before recording a refusal, and any refusal whose diagnostic still names it is a floor CONDITIONAL ON that ladder

any power-distribution area or IR-drop behaviour: this flow builds NO power distribution network and connects no straps, and the bit array's VSS pin is tied to a logic constant by insert_tiecells rather than to a rail, so every die area here is signal routing only and is a LOWER bound on that account too

bit_array_area_source: MEASURED, not declared here: read at run time from results/spice/ihp_sg13g2_bitcell/bitcell.json#rom_bitcell.cell_area_um2, and refused unless that measurement used the same revision of the layout generator this run draws with.
die_floor_probe_note: The nominal die is sized from `utilization`, so `bit array / die` is partly a restatement of a chosen constant. Each probe re-routes the identical netlist on a smaller die; the tightest that closes with zero detailed-route violations is a measured floor and the first that does not brackets it. A probe is allowed to fail: that failure is the measurement.
die_floor_probe_place_densities_note: The SECOND chosen constant, and the one the first version of this probe measured by accident. The placer's target density is `min(0.85, utilization + 0.15)`, written in tools/run_ihp_rom_macro_route.py, and every die the probe refused was refused by OpenROAD's global placer with GPL-0302 -- `Use a higher -density or re-floorplan with a larger core area` -- which names that constant as the remedy. The report nonetheless called the result a measured cell-area floor. It was a floor at 0.85. Each rung here is retried, in order, before a refusal is allowed to count; a refusal that survives the top rung while still blaming the density is recorded as conditional on this ladder rather than as a property of the design. Rungs must ascend and must all lie above the runner's 0.85 cap. Widening this ladder is legitimate; deleting it is not, and the run refuses without it.
